questions.question: In e-commerce payment systems, RTGS stands for:
questions.explanation: RTGS stands for Real Time Gross Settlement, one of the electronic fund transfer systems listed with NEFT, IMPS and UPI.

questions.question: What is the 8-bit 1's complement representation of -60?
questions.explanation: 60 = 00111100. Flipping all bits gives the 1's complement 11000011. Adding 1 (11000100) would be the 2's complement.

questions.question: Which hardware interrupt of the 8085 microprocessor is non-maskable?
questions.explanation: The 8085 has 5 hardware interrupts. TRAP is non-maskable and cannot be ignored by the CPU; RST 7.5, RST 6.5, RST 5.5 and INTR are maskable.

questions.concept: list.extend() appends each element of another list
questions.question: What is the value of lst after executing: lst = [10, 20, 30]; lst.extend([40, 50])?
questions.explanation: extend() appends each element of the given list at the end of the list. append() would instead add [40, 50] as a single nested element.

questions.concept: Alphabet is a finite set of symbols
questions.question: In automata theory, a finite set of symbols is called a(n):
questions.explanation: A symbol is a character and an alphabet is a finite set of symbols. A word is built from alphabets and a language is a set of words.

questions.concept: Number and numbering of Codd's rules
questions.question: Codd's 12 rules for a true RDBMS actually consist of how many rules, numbered how?
questions.explanation: Codd's 12 rules are a set of thirteen rules numbered 0 to 12, starting with Rule 0, the Foundation Rule.

questions.question: A user uploads a text document at 10 pages per 20 seconds. If 1 page = 1600 characters and 1 character = 8 bits, what is the data transfer rate?
questions.explanation: Bits sent = 10 x 1600 x 8 = 128000 bits in 20 seconds, so the rate is 128000 / 20 = 6400 bits per second.

questions.question: Which IoT protocol uses queues of data so that connected systems can communicate asynchronously and better handle traffic spikes?
questions.explanation: AMQP uses queues of data, enabling asynchronous communication and better handling of traffic spikes. DDS is used for real-time data exchange such as autonomous vehicles.

questions.concept: RAD as high-speed adaptation of the linear sequential model
questions.question: Which software process model is described as a high-speed adaptation of the linear sequential model?
questions.explanation: RAD (Rapid Application Development) is the high-speed adaptation of the linear sequential model and has 5 phases.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes method overloading from method overriding in Java?

options.A: Overloading needs the same signature; overriding needs a new one
options.B: Overloading spans parent and child; overriding stays in one class
options.C: Both are resolved only at runtime through dynamic binding
options.D: Overloading is resolved at compile time; overriding at runtime

questions.explanation: Overloading uses the same name with different signatures within a class and static binding at compile time. Overriding uses the same signature between parent and child classes with dynamic binding at runtime.

questions.question: Which type of virus is capable of deleting anti-virus software?
questions.explanation: A retrovirus is a virus that can delete anti-virus software. A macro virus spreads in application software, and a time bomb is a logic bomb triggered by time.

questions.concept: Firmware stored in ROM holds the BIOS
questions.question: Software that is permanently stored in ROM, helps in booting and is used to store the BIOS is called:
questions.explanation: Firmware is non-volatile software stored in ROM. It helps in booting and stores the BIOS; remote controls, TVs and ACs use it.

questions.question: A binary tree has root A, with left child B and right child C; B has a left child D. What is its postorder traversal?
questions.explanation: Postorder visits Left, Right, Root. The left subtree gives D B, then the right subtree C, then the root A: D B C A.

questions.question: Which CPU scheduling algorithm avoids starvation by giving every process a fixed time quantum?
questions.explanation: Round Robin is preemptive and gives each process a fixed time quantum, so there is no starvation. SJF and Priority scheduling can cause starvation.

questions.concept: ERP integrates and automates core business processes
questions.question: Software used by a company to manage key parts of its business by integrating and automating core business processes is called:
questions.explanation: ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) software integrates and automates core business processes of a company.

questions.question: The Myhill-Nerode theorem (1958) is used for:

options.A: Proving that a language is not context-free
options.B: Testing regularity and minimizing DFA states
options.C: Converting an NFA directly into a Turing machine
options.D: Defining the 8-tuple of a linear bounded automaton

questions.explanation: The Myhill-Nerode theorem gives necessary and sufficient conditions for a language to be regular and can minimize states in a DFA. The pumping lemma is used to show a language is not context-free.

questions.question:
Following the syllabus example, what does this Python code print?
num1 = 20
num2 = 30 - 10
print(id(num1) == id(num2))
questions.explanation: Every value in Python is an object with a unique identity returned by id(). In the syllabus example, num1 = 20 and num2 = 30 - 10 refer to the same object 20, so both ids are equal and True is printed.

questions.question: Which networking command is used to troubleshoot NetBIOS over TCP/IP issues?
questions.explanation: NBTSTAT troubleshoots NetBIOS over TCP/IP issues. NetStat shows network statistics and connections.

questions.question: Which type of database schema defines views, integrity constraints and tables, and uses ER modeling?
questions.explanation: The logical schema defines views, integrity constraints and tables and how attributes are linked; ER modeling is used here. The physical schema covers storage in files and indices.

questions.question: According to the syllabus, 5G IoT offers peak data rates of up to:
questions.explanation: 5G IoT offers peak data rates of up to 20 Gbps, with average data rates of 100+ Mbps.

questions.question: An attacker uses VoIP calls and voicemails to trick victims into revealing confidential information. This is called:
questions.explanation: Vishing (voice phishing) uses voice calls and voicemails, often placed through VoIP. Smishing uses SMS, and phishing uses emails and links.

questions.question: In Java, when a floating-point value such as 4.75 is assigned to an integer type, the fractional part is discarded and the result is 4. This is called:
questions.explanation: Truncation occurs when a floating-point value is assigned to an integer type; the fractional part is discarded, so 4.75 becomes 4. Rounding would give 5.

questions.concept: Cache performance measured by hit ratio
questions.question: The performance of cache memory is measured by its:
questions.explanation: If the requested word is found in cache it is a hit, otherwise a miss. Cache performance is measured by the hit ratio.

questions.question: Which algorithm finds shortest paths correctly even with negative weight edges, uses dynamic programming and runs in O(V x E)?
questions.explanation: Bellman-Ford handles negative weight edges, uses dynamic programming and runs in O(V x E). Dijkstra is greedy and O(E log V); Prim and Kruskal build minimum spanning trees.

questions.question: In software engineering, SRS stands for:
questions.explanation: SRS stands for Software Requirements Specification, the document describing what the software must do.
